title: Hash Maps & Sets
subtitle: Trade repeated searches for a table of precisely the information a future step needs.
variables: n and m = input lengths; u = distinct keys; k = requested count/window; L = total characters; R = number of returned items. Expected hash-table bounds assume well-distributed hashes, O(1) key hash/equality and fixed-size arithmetic; collisions can make a lookup O(u) and a build O(n²). Hashing a fresh length-l string costs O(l); Python may cache string hashes but equality still can scan characters. Tuple hashing visits all l members on each call and pays their hash costs; nested or long members need more than O(l). Python integers have bit-length-dependent costs. Space distinguishes auxiliary state from output; dict preserves insertion order, set has no ordering contract. a,b,c,d may denote independent population lengths for pair joins; u_t = distinct target symbols. Hash full-scan bounds are expected and can degrade quadratically with collisions. Count snapshots, buckets, composite keys and output slices. Templates here are iterative. u_a/u_b denote distinct keys in each input table. API costs assume CPython-like hash tables; capacities/tombstones can affect scans. Counter multiset arithmetic drops nonpositive results unlike signed balance updates. Operation table costs describe the named operation on preexisting state; executable examples also construct small fixtures and verify results, whose setup/assertion cost is not the operation cost.

contrasts: dict vs set
dict associates payloads with keys; set stores presence only. Both require hashable stable values.
set vs Counter
set ignores repetition; Counter models multiplicity and may retain zero or negative counts.
get vs defaultdict indexing
get does not insert; defaultdict[key] invokes its factory and inserts on a miss.
first vs last vs frequency
First prefix index maximizes length, recent index can minimize compatible distance, frequency counts every occurrence.
Hashing vs sorting
Hashing is expected linear with extra memory; sorting gives deterministic O(n log n) comparison work but can lose original order/indices.
Signature vs raw hash
A semantic signature must preserve equivalence; hash(signature) alone can collide and cannot replace the full key.
Window vs prefix map
A window needs monotonic repair by left removal; prefix differences handle exact sums with arbitrary signs.
dict order vs sorted order
Insertion order supports stable grouping; it does not support sorted range lookup.
At-most support vs demand coverage
At-most windows shrink while invalid; minimum-cover windows shrink while valid. Both require monotone endpoint rules.
Insertion order vs access order
Reading an ordinary dict does not change its order. LRU explicitly moves accessed keys; a hash index plus doubly linked list or OrderedDict maintains recency.
set.pop vs dict.popitem
set.pop removes an arbitrary member, not a random sample; dict.popitem removes the most recently inserted remaining key/value pair. Neither sorts by value.

decisionProcess: 0–20 seconds: Clarify output (existence, indices, ways, range length, groups), duplicates, ordering, hashability and mutation.
20–45 seconds: Choose minimal payload: presence -> set; ways -> frequency; farthest boundary -> first index; uniqueness -> last index; bijection -> two maps.

45–80 seconds: Derive prefix differences for ranges with arbitrary signs. Use windows only when left removal monotonically repairs validity; coverage and at-most support shrink in opposite situations.
80–120 seconds: State invariant, full signature and temporal boundary. Query past before publishing present; seed empty prefix when relevant.
120–180 seconds: Trace empty/self-pair/zero payload/negative sums/ties. Include expected hash and key costs, auxiliary versus output space, and sorting/bounded-alphabet alternatives.

templateDetails.observation: Reconstruct invariant: Two objects share a signature iff equivalent under the requested rule. Adaptation: 26-count tuples need validated lowercase alphabet.

templateDetails.preconditions: Sized sequences of hashable symbols; tests a bijection between observed symbols without mutation.
templateDetails.observation: Reconstruct invariant: Both maps remain inverse on processed pairs. Adaptation: Word Pattern tokenizes and checks token count.

templateDetails.preconditions: Integer iterable with arbitrary signs; returns count of nonempty contiguous ranges; empty returns 0, no mutation.
templateDetails.observation: Reconstruct invariant: freq records all earlier prefix boundaries with multiplicity. Adaptation: Pair joins lift complement counting to pairs.

templateDetails.preconditions: Integer iterable, any signs; maximum nonempty range length or 0 if none; no mutation. For equal 0/1 counts map 0 to -1 and 1 to +1.
templateDetails.observation: Reconstruct invariant: Each stored index is the earliest boundary for its state. Adaptation: Map binary 0 to -1 and 1 to +1 for balance.

templateDetails.preconditions: Integer iterable and integer nonzero k; counts nonempty divisible-sum ranges, including negative sums; no mutation.
templateDetails.observation: Reconstruct invariant: Earlier remainder frequencies enumerate all valid left boundaries. Adaptation: Minimum-length existence stores earliest remainder index.

templateDetails.preconditions: Iterable of hashable symbols; returns length, 0 when empty; map includes historical last positions, no mutation.
templateDetails.observation: Reconstruct invariant: The active window contains unique values. Adaptation: Return substring by saving endpoints and slicing once.

templateDetails.preconditions: Indexable sequence of hashable values; integer k>=0; counts nonempty ranges, k=0 returns 0. Two scans require reusable sequence, not a one-shot iterator; no mutation.
templateDetails.observation: Reconstruct invariant: Map contains positive counts exactly for the active window. Adaptation: Exactly k is atMost(k)-atMost(k-1).

templateDetails.preconditions: Integer iterable; returns longest +1 run length irrespective of original order; duplicate-insensitive, empty 0; no mutation.
templateDetails.observation: Reconstruct invariant: Every unique value belongs to exactly one scanned run. Adaptation: Not LIS: original order is discarded.

templateDetails.preconditions: Hashable iterable, integer k; frequency descending and first-appearance tie order. Invalid k raises ValueError, input unchanged. Counter consumes generators once.
templateDetails.observation: Reconstruct invariant: Higher buckets are exhausted before lower buckets contribute. Adaptation: Stable ties use first encounter; dynamic counts need another index.

templateDetails.preconditions: Unique stable hashable values; methods mutate collection, remove/insert return success bool. Uniform choice over live positions; seeded RNG aids tests, not cryptographic use. Public storage is for illustration; do not mutate it externally.
templateDetails.observation: Reconstruct invariant: position[items[i]] == i for every live slot. Adaptation: Duplicates need per-value index sets.

templateDetails.preconditions: Stable hashable iterable; bool, empty False; no mutation.
templateDetails.observation: Reconstruct invariant: seen equals distinct processed values. Adaptation: Nearby duplicates require last indices or eviction.

templateDetails.preconditions: Hashable iterables consumed once, unchanged; new output in a encounter order. Unique emits once; multiset caps multiplicity at min counts.
templateDetails.observation: Reconstruct invariant: Each balance is supplied count minus consumed count. Adaptation: Ransom Note rejects deficits; overlap emits minimum counts.

templateDetails.preconditions: Reusable numeric sequences of lengths a,b,c,d; counts index quadruples across independent populations, not distinct value quadruples. Empty -> 0, no mutation; store smaller pair product when useful.
templateDetails.observation: Reconstruct invariant: Every queried pair contributes precisely its compatible first index pairs. Adaptation: Store smaller pair product; one-array 4Sum has distinct-index constraints.

templateDetails.preconditions: Indexable hashable sequence, integer k>=0; longest length, empty/k=0 -> 0, no mutation. For at-most counting accumulate right-left+1 instead.
templateDetails.observation: Reconstruct invariant: Map contains positive counts exactly for the active window. Adaptation: Exactly k is atMost(k)-atMost(k-1).

templateDetails.preconditions: Strings with code-point multiplicity; first shortest cover or empty if impossible/empty target. Negative need denotes surplus. Only target keys stored; one final slice, no mutation.
templateDetails.observation: Reconstruct invariant: missing equals target occurrences not supplied by active window. Adaptation: Fixed-width anagrams/subsequence matching have different contracts.
